q-334767.name: Question 1
q-334767.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-5x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-5y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the general solution to the system of ODEs above?

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-5t} & t{e}^{-5t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-5t}\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}].$*
q-334767.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$
{Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-5t} & t{e}^{-5t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-5t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c \\  & ={e}^{At}\,c \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-5t} & t{e}^{-5t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-5t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-5t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{-5t} \\ {e}^{-5t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-5t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-5t},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.$

q-334769.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=8x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=8y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the general solution to the system of ODEs above?

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{8t} & t{e}^{8t} \\ 0 & {e}^{8t}\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}].$*
q-334769.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$
{Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{8t} & t{e}^{8t} \\ 0 & {e}^{8t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c \\  & ={e}^{At}\,c \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{8t} & t{e}^{8t} \\ 0 & {e}^{8t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{8t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{8t} \\ {e}^{8t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{8t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{8t},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.$

q-334780.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-11y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=11x(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the general solution to the system of ODEs above?

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(11t) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(11t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(11t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(11t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -11 \\ 11 & 0\end{aligned}].$*
q-334780.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -11 \\ 11 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -11 \\ 11 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$
{Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(11t) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(11t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(11t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(11t)\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c \\  & ={e}^{At}\,c \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(11t) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(11t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(11t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(11t)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(11t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(11t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(11t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(11t)\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.$

\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=2x(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(-2) \\ y(-2)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].$*
q-335451.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)c={e}^{At}\,c,
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting $t={t}_{0},$ we have 

$$
x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c,
$$

and since ${e}^{At}$ is invertible for all $t,$ we have

$$
c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}).
$$

Plugging the above back into our expression for $x(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}) \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{A(t-(-2))}\,x(-2) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(2(t+2)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(2(t+2)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(2(t+2)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(2(t+2))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2(t+2)) \\ -2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(2(t+2))\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
